The other side's claims could be priced from the record but yours could not, so a net figure would show only what you might pay. prediction.likelyOutcome: Cumberland is well positioned to substantially defeat Blackwing's $167,050 TI-allowance counterclaim given the industry-custom affidavit and Blackwing's own concession that receipts were never submitted, and likely holds the stronger position on liability for unpaid rent generally -- but the self-help/statutory-notice declaratory judgment count and the failure-to-deliver/vent-hood allegations create real, unresolved risk to the eviction claim and could support a rent abatement defense that isn't quantifiable on this record. Because no rent figure or arrears total appears anywhere in the materials, Cumberland's own affirmative recovery cannot be computed, so this assessment prices only the known TI exposure rather than a full net position.

outcome.description: The trial court granted the landlord summary judgment on its eviction and breach-of-contract claims, restored it to possession by writ (tenant evicted April 6, 2023), and after a damages hearing awarded Cumberland $444,055.13; it later granted summary judgment against all of Blackwing's counterclaims, including the $167,050 tenant-improvement claim. No attorneys' fee award is mentioned. The Eighth District affirmed.

source.caseName: Cumberland Lakefront B, LLC v. Blackwing, LLC, et al.
source.court: Court of Appeals of Ohio, Eighth Appellate District, Cuyahoga County (appeal from Cuyahoga County Court of Common Pleas Nos. CV-21-953921 and CV-21-953922)
source.excerptNote: Verbatim from the opinion's opening factual/procedural recitation and from its discussion of the tenant's counterclaims (which is where the opinion sets out both sides' contentions and the Pace affidavit). Removed: every sentence stating that the trial court granted summary judgment, granted possession, issued the writ, found liability, held a damages hearing and the amount awarded, deemed property abandoned, or granted summary judgment on the counterclaims; the prior-appeal dismissal history; the appellate court's analysis and conclusions. Two retained sentences refer to Blackwing's position 'on appeal' but state only its contention and demand, not any result. The opinion contains no rent figures.
